source: Johor (Set 3) 2026 · Paper 2 · Part 2 Q2 · Essay, 125–150 words
paragraphs: In this digital era, cyberbullying has become an alarming issue. One example of cyberbullying on social media is leaving derogatory remarks under a classmate's photo to humiliate him or her. Such comments can be detrimental to the victim's mental well-being.

First and foremost, online bullying happens because netizens can remain anonymous behind fake accounts. Believing they will never be caught, they type cruel words they would never say face to face. Furthermore, bullies cannot see their victims' reactions. As a result, they fail to realise how deeply their words hurt.

Students can stop cyberbullying by reporting abusive posts instead of being silent bystanders. This allows harmful content to be removed quickly. Moreover, they can reach out to the victims and offer emotional support. This helps victims regain their confidence. In a nutshell, if every student plays a part, we can foster a safe environment in the digital world.
